title: Mercy outruns anger
hookLine: Allah wrote, My mercy prevails over My anger (Bukhari; Muslim)

lines: SO SHE WON'T STEP ON HER FOAL.
WHICH COMES FIRST, MERCY OR ANGER?
cards: Watch a horse with a newborn foal. The foal is wobbly, all legs, tangled up underneath her. And the mare, a huge animal, lifts one hoof and holds it in the air, carefully, so she won't step on her baby.
It's a small, ordinary thing, easy to miss. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ used exactly that picture, the lifted hoof, to explain where mercy comes from.

And Bukhari and Muslim record another saying, about something written before anything else existed: which comes first when mercy and anger meet. Two names so far from the root r-h-m. Now the root itself: rahmah, mercy.

teach.b: First, the writing. The Prophet said that when Allah created the creation, He wrote in a Book that is with Him, above the Throne: My mercy prevails over My anger. The reports use two different verbs.

In one, ghalabat: My mercy overcomes My anger, wins against it. In the other, sabaqat: My mercy outruns My anger, gets there first, like a runner leaving the other behind. Mercy is stronger, and it's faster.
In another hadith the Prophet said Allah made mercy in one hundred parts. He kept ninety-nine with Himself and sent one part down to the earth.
From that one part, every creature is merciful to every other: parents to children, friend to friend, the mare lifting her hoof from her foal.
Everything tender you have ever seen in this world, all of it together, is one percent. Now the root.
Rahmah comes from r-h-m, and the same root gives rahim, the womb. Bukhari records a saying that the womb, rahim, is a branch of ar-Rahman.
Some readers hear in that root a mercy shaped like the place where a person is first held, protected and fed before they can do anything to deserve it.
Muslims also believe Allah's anger is real, and the Qur'an speaks of it. The saying doesn't erase it.
It puts it in order: when the two meet, mercy wins, and mercy got there first.

how: The hadith that Allah's mercy prevails over His anger is quoted to encourage hope and forgiveness, and the hundred parts of mercy turn up in sermons and in teaching children kindness to people and animals.

o: the gentle tone used in reciting prayers
mercy, from the root that also gives womb
a feeling of pity that excuses wrongdoing

games.q: what's inside the sayings — tap the pairs.
p: the womb, from the same root

s: the hadith says Allah has no anger
it says mercy prevails over His anger; both are real, and mercy wins.
all the mercy on earth is one part of a hundred
ninety-nine are kept with Allah (Bukhari; Muslim).
rahmah and rahim, the womb, share a root

games.q: Allah made mercy in a hundred parts. how many did He send to the earth?
games.why: one. from it, every creature is merciful to another, even the mare lifting her hoof. the other ninety-nine are kept with Him.

practice: Think of someone who has annoyed you recently, and notice the judgment arrive, the little story about what kind of person they are.
Before you finish that story, let mercy get there first: picture them as someone's child, once held and fed before they'd done anything at all, or picture the mare lifting her hoof.
You don't have to agree with them; just let mercy run ahead of the verdict for one breath, then another.

wordCard.voice: Rahmah. Mercy, from the root that also gives the womb: the mercy Allah wrote prevails over His anger. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: mercy, from r-h-m, the root that also gives rahim, the womb.

carryVoice: Your line: mercy wins. It was written down before anything else. Day two hundred thirty-seven, done.
